verdict.rationale: MotherDuck's remote MCP server and Dives let users ask natural-language questions and get answers and visualizations without writing SQL, and the agent can explore schemas. Grounding comes from Guides, markdown documents that capture the org's metric definitions and join conventions so agents produce accurate SQL. Governance comes from read-only restriction of the assistant and include-pattern scoped Shares. This counts as partial rather than full because Guides are free-text context the external agent may or may not follow, not an enforced semantic layer, and nothing shows answers are actually kept from hallucinated joins. Missing for 10: an enforced semantic layer or metric model that constrains generated SQL, a governed business-user experience independent of a third-party AI client, and hands-on or independent evidence of answer accuracy.
